rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 is the best so far (220.09). Its oval track finished in 6 of 20 trials at a mean time of 1.875 s, so speed 1.0 can complete a lap. The s-bend and slalom tracks still ended almost entirely off track (progress 0.26 and 0.17). max_error sits at about 0.06 m, the off-track floor, while rms_error is about 0.03 m. The robot tracks on average and then makes one large excursion that loses the tape. Steering oscillation (0.23 to 0.27) is now higher than before, so the response is not yet well damped. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 for every allowed body width, so geometry cannot widen it. Reducing the excursion is the lever.

Changes: (1) Sensors moved forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 m. Seeing the line earlier gives the controller more lead on bends and cuts the phase lag that lets the error grow on the s-bend and slalom. (2) base_speed lowered from 1.0 to 0.9. Lateral error scales with speed in curves, and the s-bend and slalom are the failing tracks. Oval should still finish, since finished runs averaged 1.875 s. (3) kp kept at 2.0 and kd at 1.0, because these were the best-observed controller values and changing them together with the sensor move would confound the result. (4) Geometry is otherwise unchanged (x spacing 0.02 m over -0.04 to +0.04, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.16 x 0.12 m, wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m). ki stays at 0 and line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer off-track exits on s-bend and slalom, with progress rising from about 0.2 toward 0.35 or more and scores above 220 if the oval still finishes. The main risk is that the forward sensors and lower speed slow the response enough to hurt rms_error. The revision rounds should check this against the Evaluator's critique.
